In Islamic art, the color blue is used extensively, notably in the blue fibrations found in the walls of the Dome of the Rock, considered one of the holiest sites in Islam. In Sufi poetry, the color blue is repeatedly used as a metaphor for spiritual matters, with Rumi in particular using the metaphor of the 'Blue Ocean' to describe the spiritual realm, beyond the ordinary world of senses and materiality. Thus, the name Nilabh, with its allusion to the spiritual significance of blue in Islamic and Sufi traditions, offers a sublime connotation, evoking a sense of the divine and the sacred, and inviting reflection on the spiritual journey towards self-understanding and growth.
